title: The Anupāya perspective dissolves the ground question: the two aspects were never separate

question.tension_point: TĀ 2 (Anupāya) reveals that the two-aspect structure was never truly separate. The entire reflexivity debate — whether structure is self-grounding, grounded in vimarśa, or groundless — operates from within a separation that Anupāya reveals as illusory. Does this dissolve the debate or deepen it?

pratijna.proposition: The Anupāya perspective reveals that the reflexivity debate operates from within a separation (subject/object, ground/grounded) that is not ultimately real. From the No Means perspective, the question 'what grounds the two aspects?' dissolves because the two aspects were never separate.
pratijna.what_it_claims: Seven probes have progressively deepened the reflexivity question. The Anupāya finding is the deepest: it doesn't answer the question but reveals that the question presupposes a separation that doesn't exist at the ultimate level.

evidence.claim: TĀ 2: 'Of what use can any means of realization be with regard to this Supreme Lord Who is self-luminous Light and our own Self?' Consciousness needs no means because it IS self-luminous.
PS(V) 1.9ab: cognition has two appearances. Self-awareness is the result.
Ñāṇavīra: viññāṇa is anidassana — pointing to no ground.

examples.scenario: TĀ 2: 'What use are means to the Self-luminous? It cannot attain itself, illumine itself, or reveal itself — it IS itself.'
examples.what_it_shows: The question 'what grounds the two aspects?' arises from the perspective of separation. From Anupāya, the two aspects were never separate.

examples.scenario: Each EO in the trajectory reframed the question. EO v7 is the reframing of the reframing: the debate itself is the symptom.
examples.what_it_shows: The trajectory shows progressive refinement toward a question that may not have an answer within the framework that generated it.

upanaya.application: Seven probes have progressively refined the reflexivity question. Each probe produced a deeper understanding. The Anupāya finding reveals that the deepest understanding may be that the question dissolves rather than resolves.
cruxes: Does the Anupāya perspective genuinely dissolve the debate, or is it itself a position within the debate?
Can the three positions (self-grounding, vimarśa-grounded, groundless) be seen as expressions of the same reality at different levels of separation?

nigamana.best_current_answer: The reflexivity debate between Dignāga, Abhinavagupta, and Ñāṇavīra has been refined through 7 EOs to a point where the deepest probe reveals that the question may dissolve rather than resolve. The three positions describe the same reality at different levels of perceived separation: Dignāga at the level of cognition (separation appears real), Abhinavagupta at the level of recognition (separation is recognized as within consciousness), Ñāṇavīra at the level of cessation (the conceit that seeks separation has ceased), and Anupāya at the level where separation was never actual.
nigamana.scope: The positions are compatible across levels. Which level is 'correct' depends on the question being asked.

candidates.name: Self-grounding structure (Dignāga)
candidates.position: Cognition is two-aspect. No ground needed.

candidates.name: Vimarśa as ground (Abhinavagupta)
candidates.position: The Heart is the foundation of consciousness.

candidates.name: Groundless reflexivity (Ñāṇavīra)
candidates.position: The search for a ground is asmimāna.

candidates.name: Anupāya dissolution (Abhinavagupta)
candidates.position: The separation the question presupposes was never real.

state_of_play.summary: Seven probes have produced four perspectives on reflexivity: (1) Dignāga describes cognition, (2) Abhinavagupta describes the nature of consciousness, (3) Ñāṇavīra describes the cessation of the ground-seeking conceit, (4) Anupāya reveals the question presupposes a separation that isn't ultimately real. These are not competing — they describe different levels of the same reality.
state_of_play.what_survives: All four perspectives survive as coherent descriptions at different levels.
state_of_play.what_is_weakened: The framing as a resolvable debate between competing positions.
state_of_play.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that one tradition is describing a different phenomenon than the others, making the level-compatibility reading invalid.
open_cruxes: Are the four perspectives compatible or in tension?
Does the compatibility reading reduce each tradition's distinctive claims?
next_tests: The reflexivity question has been fully characterized. Move to Q17 or a fresh question from the 72.
